name: Arnold Schwarzenegger
milestone_by_age_26: Won the NABBA Mr. Universe title in 1967 at age 20, becoming the youngest winner in the competition's history, and went on to win Mr. Olympia in 1970 at age 23.
early_history_summary: Schwarzenegger began lifting weights at age 15 in Thal, Austria, choosing bodybuilding over football at 14. He trained fanatically, breaking into his local gym on weekends. After serving in the Austrian Army in 1965, he won Mr. Europe and competed at the 1966 NABBA Mr. Universe, placing second. In 1967 he won Mr. Universe at age 20, then moved to the U.S. in 1968 to train at Gold's Gym under Joe Weider, winning Mr. Olympia in 1970.
family_context_summary: Son of Gustav Schwarzenegger, local police chief in Thal, Austria. The household was strict and modest; Arnold had a difficult relationship with his father. Not wealthy by any measure.
parent_family_domain_summary: Father encouraged sports participation and had done curling himself, but had no bodybuilding expertise. No domain-specific transfer documented.
primary_early_advantage_tags: extraordinary physical response to training, Reg Park mentorship, Joe Weider sponsorship, Gold's Gym access, youngest Mr. Universe
evidence_summary: Schwarzenegger's extraordinary physical talent was evident from his teens — he won Mr. Universe at 20, the youngest ever. His mentor Reg Park (childhood idol turned friend) and Joe Weider (bodybuilding magazine tycoon who brought him to the U.S.) provided critical guidance and opportunity. He trained with fanatical intensity, breaking into gyms on weekends. His modest Austrian background offered no financial platform, but his physical prodigy status and mentorship network catalyzed his early dominance.

name: Nobuyoshi Araki
milestone_by_age_26: Won the Taiyō Prize and the Sun Prize for photography in 1964 at age 24, establishing early recognition in the Japanese photography world.
early_history_summary: Araki studied film and photography at Chiba University from 1959, graduating in 1963. He then worked at the advertising agency Dentsu, where he met his future wife Yōko Aoki. In 1964 he won two national photography prizes — the Taiyō Prize and the Sun Prize — marking his first professional recognition as a photographer.
family_context_summary: Born in Tokyo. Family background and financial status are not documented in reviewed sources.
primary_early_advantage_tags: Chiba University photography program, Dentsu advertising agency, Tokyo art scene
evidence_summary: Araki studied photography at Chiba University and worked at Dentsu, Japan's largest advertising agency, providing him with both technical training and professional equipment access. Winning the Taiyō Prize and Sun Prize in 1964 at age 24 marked his first material recognition. His family background is not documented in reviewed sources, so no early advantage scores beyond institutional and geographic proximity can be substantiated.

name: Carlos Ghosn
milestone_by_age_26: Ineligible: Ghosn began his professional career at Michelin in 1978 as a trainee at age 24. His first leadership role — plant manager at Le Puy-en-Velay — came in 1981 at age 27. No material milestone by age 26 is documented.
early_history_summary: Ghosn grew up in Lebanon and Brazil, attending the Jesuit Collège Notre Dame de Jamhour in Beirut. He graduated from École Polytechnique in 1974 and École des Mines de Paris in 1978, then joined Michelin as a trainee. His career advanced steadily but his first significant management role came at 27.
family_context_summary: Grandson of Bichara Ghosn, a Lebanese immigrant entrepreneur in Brazil who headed several companies. Father Jorge was a diamond trader and airline industry worker convicted of murdering a priest in 1960. Family was affluent but disrupted; parents separated and Carlos was raised partly in Lebanon.
parent_family_domain_summary: Grandfather was an entrepreneur in rubber trade, agricultural products, and aviation. Father worked in diamond trading and airlines. Business background in family but not directly in automotive industry.
evidence_summary: Ghosn attended elite French institutions (École Polytechnique, École des Mines) and came from a business-oriented Lebanese-Brazilian family. However, his professional career at Michelin began as a trainee in 1978 at age 24, and his first management role came at 27. No material milestone by age 26 is documented.

name: Rowan Atkinson
milestone_by_age_26: First won national attention at the Edinburgh Festival Fringe in August 1976 at age 21 with the Oxford Revue, leading to a BBC Radio 3 series and the landmark BBC2 sketch show Not the Nine O'Clock News in October 1979 at age 24, for which he won a BAFTA in 1981.
early_history_summary: Atkinson studied electrical engineering at Newcastle University, then pursued an MSc at The Queen's College, Oxford. At Oxford he joined the Oxford University Dramatic Society and the Etceteras revue group, meeting writer Richard Curtis and composer Howard Goodall. His Edinburgh Fringe performance in 1976 attracted BBC producer John Lloyd, who cast him in Not the Nine O'Clock News in 1979.
family_context_summary: Born in Consett, County Durham, to a middle-class family. His brother Rodney Atkinson is a political activist and academic. Family was supportive but not wealthy; Atkinson attended state schools before university.
parent_family_domain_summary: Not documented in reviewed sources. No evidence of family connections in entertainment or comedy.
primary_early_advantage_tags: Oxford University, Richard Curtis collaboration, BBC pipeline, Edinburgh Fringe, alternative comedy wave
evidence_summary: Atkinson's path was shaped by elite institutional access — Newcastle and Oxford universities provided the platform for his comedy development. At Oxford he met Richard Curtis, his key writing collaborator, and performed at the Edinburgh Fringe in 1976, which led to the BBC's Not the Nine O'Clock News in 1979. The alternative comedy movement of late-1970s Britain was a structural wave he rode. His distinctive physical comedy style was evident early but family background in entertainment is not documented.

name: Jo Nesbø
milestone_by_age_26: Ineligible: Nesbø's band Di Derre was founded in 1992 (age 32) with their breakthrough album in 1994 (age 34). His first novel was published in 1997 (age 37). No material milestone by age 26 is documented.
early_history_summary: Nesbø grew up in Molde, Norway, played football for Molde FK until a knee injury ended his career, and graduated from the Norwegian School of Economics. He worked as a stockbroker and journalist before forming Di Derre at 32 and publishing his first novel at 37.
family_context_summary: Mother Kirsten was a librarian; father Per Nesbø fought for Germany on the Eastern Front in WWII, received a prison sentence, and struggled financially working odd jobs. Family was not affluent.
parent_family_domain_summary: Mother was a librarian, providing literary environment. Father had no domain-relevant background and struggled financially.
evidence_summary: Nesbø's path to fame was late: he played football and worked as a stockbroker before forming Di Derre at 32 and publishing his first crime novel at 37. His mother was a librarian and his father struggled financially after a WWII-related prison sentence. No material milestone by age 26 is documented.

name: John Holmes
milestone_by_age_26: Ineligible: Holmes began appearing in adult films in the late 1960s and did nude modeling from 1969, but his career-making Johnny Wadd film series did not begin until 1971 when he was 27. No material milestone by age 26 is documented.
early_history_summary: Holmes grew up in small-town Ohio in a turbulent household with an alcoholic stepfather. He served in the U.S. Army in West Germany and worked various jobs before drifting into the underground adult film industry in the late 1960s. His breakout role as Johnny Wadd came in 1971 at age 27.
family_context_summary: Born John Curtis Estes in Ashville, Ohio. Mother Mary June was a devout Southern Baptist; stepfather Edgar was an alcoholic. Turbulent, poor household. Father Carl Estes was a railroad worker whose name was left blank on the birth certificate.
parent_family_domain_summary: Not documented in reviewed sources. No evidence of family connections in entertainment.
evidence_summary: Holmes came from a troubled, impoverished background in rural Ohio. He drifted into the underground adult film industry in the late 1960s but his career-defining Johnny Wadd series began in 1971 at age 27. No material milestone by age 26 is documented; his fame and prolific output came after 26.

name: Paolo Rossi
milestone_by_age_26: Won the Serie B Golden Boot with 21 goals for Vicenza in the 1976-77 season at age 20-21, led Vicenza to Serie A promotion, then became the first player to top the scoring charts in Serie B and Serie A in consecutive seasons with 24 goals in 1977-78, and played for Italy at the 1978 World Cup at age 22.
early_history_summary: Rossi joined Juventus youth system at 16 in 1972 but was injury-prone, requiring three knee operations. After loan spells at Como, he joined Vicenza on loan in 1976 where coach Fabbri moved him from the wing to centre-forward. He immediately won the Serie B Golden Boot, then topped Serie A scoring the next season, earning a world-record co-ownership transfer fee and a call-up to Italy's 1978 World Cup squad.
family_context_summary: Youngest son of Vittorio Rossi, a local laundryman and keen amateur footballer, from Prato in Tuscany. Modest working-class background.
parent_family_domain_summary: Father was a keen amateur footballer, providing early exposure to the sport, but no professional football connections documented.
primary_early_advantage_tags: Juventus youth system, Italian football pipeline, Coach Fabbri positional change, Serie B Golden Boot, World Cup 1978
evidence_summary: Rossi's early career was built on the Juventus youth system pipeline, which he entered at 16. Though injury-prone and initially a winger, coach Fabbri at Vicenza converted him to centre-forward, unlocking his goal-scoring ability. He won the Serie B Golden Boot at 20-21 and topped Serie A the next season — a historic consecutive double. His father was a laundryman and amateur footballer; the family was working-class. Three knee operations in his teens created significant adversity that he overcame.

name: Kate Bush
milestone_by_age_26: Topped the UK singles chart for four weeks in March 1978 at age 19 with her debut single 'Wuthering Heights,' becoming the first female artist to achieve a UK number one with a fully self-written song; her debut album The Kick Inside sold over a million copies.
early_history_summary: Bush began writing songs at age 11, taught herself piano, and grew up in a musical household in Kent. Family friend Ricky Hopper passed her demo to Pink Floyd guitarist David Gilmour, who financed a professional demo recording when she was 16. EMI signed her, gave her a large advance, and she spent two years studying interpretive dance before releasing 'Wuthering Heights' at 19.
family_context_summary: Born to a middle-class family in Bexleyheath, Kent. Father Paddy was a doctor and amateur pianist; mother was an amateur traditional Irish dancer. Two older brothers were heavily involved in music and poetry. Artistic household that encouraged creative development.
parent_family_domain_summary: Father was an amateur pianist and mother an amateur Irish dancer; both older brothers were deeply involved in music. Family provided a rich musical environment and supported her artistic development from childhood.
primary_early_advantage_tags: David Gilmour mentorship, EMI contract at 16, musical family, interpretive dance training, UK pop chart wave
evidence_summary: Bush's extraordinary songwriting talent emerged at 11, but the critical catalyst was David Gilmour of Pink Floyd, who personally financed her professional demo recording and connected her to EMI. Her family was middle-class and deeply musical — father a doctor and pianist, mother a dancer, brothers in music. EMI signed her at 16 and gave her a large advance for dance training. Her debut single 'Wuthering Heights' topped the UK chart at 19, making her the first female artist with a self-written number one. The combination of mentorship, family musical environment, and label investment created a uniquely accelerated path.

name: Mark Webber
milestone_by_age_26: Made his Formula One debut at the 2002 Australian Grand Prix on March 3, 2002 at age 25, finishing fifth and scoring points — becoming the 51st driver in F1 history to score on debut and the first Australian F1 driver since 1994.
early_history_summary: Webber began karting at age 12-13 in Queanbeyan, Australia, buying a go-kart from a school friend's father. His father leased a petrol station and worked long hours to fund his racing. He won regional karting championships in 1992-93, moved to car racing in 1994, and progressed through Australian Formula Ford, British Formula Ford, FIA GT Championship with Mercedes AMG, and International Formula 3000 before reaching F1 in 2002.
family_context_summary: Born to middle-class parents in Queanbeyan, New South Wales. Father was a motorcycle enthusiast who leased a petrol station and worked long hours at a car dealer to fund Mark's karting. Maternal grandfather had a 2,500-acre farm where Mark drove motorbikes from age 4-5.
parent_family_domain_summary: Father was a motorcycle enthusiast and worked in fuel/automotive sectors, providing early exposure to motorsport culture. No professional racing background in family.
primary_early_advantage_tags: karting from age 12, father funded racing, Van Diemen factory team, Mercedes AMG, moved to UK motorsport hub
evidence_summary: Webber's path to F1 was built on years of progressive racing from karting in rural Australia to European formula racing. His father made significant financial sacrifices, leasing a petrol station and working extra jobs to fund karting. Andy Lawson built karts around Webber's frame, and Ralph Firman Sr. signed him to the Van Diemen factory team. Moving to London in 1995 placed him in the UK motorsport hub. His F1 debut at 25, scoring points for Minardi, was the culmination of a decade of systematic progression through racing categories.

name: Gianluigi Buffon
milestone_by_age_26: Made his Serie A debut for Parma on November 19, 1995 at age 17, keeping a clean sheet against reigning champions AC Milan, and by 26 had become a World Cup-winning goalkeeper, Serie A champion, and the world's most expensive goalkeeper transfer.
early_history_summary: Buffon joined Parma's youth system in 1991 at age 13. He made his Serie A debut at 17 in November 1995 when first-choice keeper Luca Bucci was injured, keeping a clean sheet against AC Milan's star-studded attack including Baggio and Weah. He became Parma's starting goalkeeper the following season and won the Coppa Italia, UEFA Cup, and Italian Super Cup with Parma before his world-record transfer to Juventus in 2001.
family_context_summary: Born in Carrara, Tuscany. Both parents were physical education teachers — mother Maria Stella Masocco was a discus thrower and father Adriano was a weightlifter. Two sisters were also athletes. Athletic family environment with strong sporting genes.
parent_family_domain_summary: Both parents were PE teachers and competitive athletes (discus thrower and weightlifter). Family provided a deeply athletic environment and genetic predisposition for physical performance, though not football-specific.
primary_early_advantage_tags: Parma youth system, athletic family, prodigy debut at 17, Italian football pipeline, Nevio Scala mentorship
evidence_summary: Buffon's extraordinary debut at 17 — keeping a clean sheet against AC Milan's world-class attack — was immediately recognized as exceptional by legends like Dino Zoff. Both parents were competitive athletes and PE teachers, providing a strong athletic foundation. The Parma youth system, one of Italy's finest academies, gave him elite training from age 13. Coach Nevio Scala's decision to debut him at 17 against Milan was a pivotal mentorship moment. His athletic family background and the Italian football pipeline combined with his prodigy-level talent to create an accelerated path to the top.

name: George Weah
milestone_by_age_26: Signed for AS Monaco in 1988 at age 22 after being discovered by Arsène Wenger, was named African Footballer of the Year in 1989 at age 23, won the Coupe de France with Monaco in 1991, and helped Monaco reach the European Cup Winners' Cup final in 1992 before signing for PSG at age 26.
early_history_summary: Weah grew up in the Clara Town slum of Monrovia, Liberia, raised by his grandmother after his parents separated. He played street football and climbed through Liberian local clubs — Bong Range United, Mighty Barrolle, Invincible Eleven — before joining Cameroonian club Tonnerre Yaoundé in 1987. Cameroon coach Claude Le Roy recommended him to Arsène Wenger at Monaco, who signed him for £12,000 in 1988.
family_context_summary: Born in Monrovia, Liberia, and raised in the Clara Town slum. Father William was a mechanic; mother Anna Quaye Weah died early. Raised by paternal grandmother Emma Klonjlaleh Brown. Extreme poverty; member of the Kru ethnic group from one of Liberia's poorest areas.
parent_family_domain_summary: No football or professional connections in family. Father was a mechanic. No domain-relevant transfer documented.
primary_early_advantage_tags: slum upbringing, street football, Arsène Wenger mentorship, Claude Le Roy recommendation, African Footballer of Year 1989
evidence_summary: Weah's path from Monrovia slums to European football was extraordinary. He had no family resources, no training facilities, and no football connections — he learned the game on dusty streets. Cameroon coach Claude Le Roy spotted him and recommended him to Arsène Wenger at Monaco, who became a father figure and mentor. Wenger's sustained coaching was transformative. Weah was named African Footballer of the Year at 23 in 1989. His extreme poverty and outsider status created the urgency and distinctive style that propelled him, but Wenger's mentorship was the critical catalyst that brought him to European football.

name: Tim Cook
milestone_by_age_26: Ineligible: Cook graduated from Auburn University in 1982 and joined IBM's personal computer business as a junior employee. He earned an MBA from Duke University in 1988 while working at IBM. His significant leadership roles came later in his career.
family_context_summary: Born in Mobile, Alabama, and grew up in Robertsdale. Father Donald was a shipyard worker; mother Geraldine worked at a pharmacy. Working-class family in rural Alabama.
parent_family_domain_summary: Not documented in reviewed sources. No evidence of family connections in technology or business.
evidence_summary: Cook came from a working-class family in rural Alabama — father a shipyard worker, mother a pharmacy worker. He graduated from Auburn University in 1982 and joined IBM as a junior employee in the PC business. His rise to director of North American fulfillment at IBM came years later, and his transformative career move to Apple came in 1998 at age 38. No material milestone by age 26 is documented.
